parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Beams of protons, neutrons and electrons behave differently in an electric field due to their differing properties.

The diagram shows the path of a beam of electrons in an electric field.

Add and label lines to represent the paths of beams of protons and neutrons in the same field.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
The fifth to eighth ionisation energies of three elements in the third period of the Periodic Table are given. The symbols used for reference are **not** the actual symbols of the elements.

|  | ionisation energies, $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |  |  |  |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| {{blocked}} | fifth | sixth | seventh | eighth |
| **X** | 6274 | 21269 | 25398 | 29855 |
| **Y** | 7012 | 8496 | 27107 | 31671 |
| **Z** | 6542 | 9362 | 11018 | 33606 |
parts.text: State and explain the group number of element **Y**.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain the general trend in **first** ionisation energies across the third period.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why the **first** ionisation energy of element **Y** is less than that of element **X**.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Complete the electronic configuration of element **Z**.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
A sample of strontium exists as a mixture of four isotopes. Information about three of these isotopes is given in the table.

| mass number | 86 | 87 | 88 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| abundance | 9.86% | 7.00% | 82.58% |
parts.text: Calculate the abundance of the fourth isotope.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
The relative atomic mass of this sample of strontium is 87.71.

Calculate the mass number of the fourth isotope.
